question_text: What is one part of the judicial branch?
lead_in: Either of these works (you only need one):

why_it_matters.text: 'Judicial' means relating to courts or judges. The judicial branch is the system of courts that interprets the law. At the top is the Supreme Court — the final word on every federal legal question. Below it are the federal district courts and courts of appeals.

fun_fact.text: The Constitution requires only one court — the Supreme Court. Article III says 'one supreme Court, and such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.' Every other federal court — district courts, courts of appeals — exists only because Congress chose to create them, starting with the Judiciary Act of 1789.
